# strata-cli

`charly strata` drives a running Strata engine from the HOST over its own HTTP API — the
same API your clients use. It is a `command:strata` plugin, talks plain HTTP, and therefore
works identically compiled-in or out-of-process with no reverse channel.

## Endpoint resolution

`--server <url>` > the engine's own `HOST`/`PORT` (a container bind address
(`0.0.0.0`) is mapped to `127.0.0.1` for client use) > `http://127.0.0.1:8080`. A schemeless
value gets `http://` prepended. That is the SERVER ROOT — the management routes live there,
while the candy's provided `STRATA_BASE_URL` is the OpenAI-compatible API root under `/v1`.

A charly deployment auto-allocates the host port, so `charly status <name>` is the authority
on what to pass.

## Command tree

- `charly strata version` — `GET /health`: status, model, `max_context`, and whether a key
  is set (`api_key`). Answered BEFORE the API-key gate, so it needs no secret.
- `charly strata status` — `GET /status`.
- `charly strata models` — `GET /v1/models`, the OpenAI-compatible list (there is NO
  management `/models` route).
- `charly strata props` — `GET /props`, the loaded model's properties.
- `charly strata config [<key>]` — `GET /config`. With no argument it prints the engine's
  whole published catalogue; with a key it prints that one value. The catalogue is the
  engine's own, so nothing here hard-codes a key name that could drift.
- `charly strata metrics` — `GET /metrics`.

The API key is read from `API_KEY` (the engine's own name) or `STRATA_API_KEY` (the name a
charly deployment supplies).

## What it deliberately does NOT do

- **No `config set`.** At the pinned engine version a config save replaces the volume's
  run-config symlink with a regular file inside the image, so the volume never changes and
  the edit dies with the container (upstream #2547, still open). Non-runtime-editable
  configuration belongs in the deployment's `env:`, which is the layer's design.
- **No `logs`.** The engine serves no logs route at all, and `charly logs <name>` already
  owns viewing a deployment's output — a second surface would be a duplicate.
